arxiv-2205-13723.title: DLTTA: Dynamic Learning Rate for Test-time Adaptation on Cross-domain Medical Images Thanks: Hongzheng Yang is with the Department of Artificial Intelligence, Beihang University, Beijing, China. This work was done when H.Z. Yang did internship with CUHK. Cheng Chen, Meirui Jiang, Quande Liu, Jianfen
arxiv-2205-13723.creator: Hongzheng Yang, Cheng Chen, Meirui Jiang
arxiv-2205-13723.description: Abstract Test-time adaptation (TTA) has increasingly been an important topic to efficiently tackle the cross-domain distribution shift at test time for medical images from different institutions. Previous TTA methods have a common limitation of using a fixed learning rate for all the test samples.

arxiv-2302-03108.title: Reduction for asynchronous Boolean networks: elimination of negatively autoregulated components
arxiv-2302-03108.creator: Robert Schwieger, Elisa Tonello
arxiv-2302-03108.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Robert Schwieger, Elisa Tonello. To simplify the analysis of Boolean networks, a reduction in the number of components is often considered. A popular reduction method consists in eliminating components that are not autoregulated, using variable substitution. In this work, we show how this method can be extended, for asynchronous dynamics of Boolean networks, to the elimination of vertices that have a negative autoregulation, and study the effects on the dynamics and interaction structure.

arxiv-2312-13591.title: Spectrum of the molecular pentaquarks
arxiv-2312-13591.creator: Bo Wang, Kan Chen, Lu Meng, Shi-Lin Zhu
arxiv-2312-13591.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bo Wang, Kan Chen, Lu Meng, Shi-Lin Zhu. We investigate the mass spectrum of the molecular pentaquarks composed of a baryon and a meson. We establish the underlying relations among the near-threshold interactions of the molecular tetraquark and pentaquark systems.

arxiv-2312-17436.title: Nonthermal electron-photon steady states in open cavity quantum materials
arxiv-2312-17436.creator: R. Flores-Calderón, Md Mursalin Islam, Michele Pini, Francesco Piazza
arxiv-2312-17436.description: Abstract Coupling a system to two different baths can lead to novel phenomena escaping the constraints of thermal equilibrium. In quantum materials inside optical cavities, this feature can be exploited as electrons and cavity-photons are easily pulled away from their mutual equilibrium, even in the steady state. This offers new routes for a non-invasive control of material properties and functionalities.

arxiv-2403-10591.title: Effective time–dependent temperature for fermionic master equations beyond the Markov and the secular approximations
arxiv-2403-10591.creator: Lukas Litzba, Eric Kleinherbers, Jürgen König, Ralf Schützhold, Nikodem Szpak
arxiv-2403-10591.description: Abstract We consider a fermionic quantum system exchanging particles with an environment at a fixed temperature and study its reduced evolution by means of a Redfield–I equation with time–dependent (non–Markovian) coefficients. We find that the description can be efficiently reduced to a standard–form Redfield–II equation, however, with a time–dependent effective bath temperature obeying a universal law.

arxiv-2403-14436.title: Spectral Methods for Quantum Optimal Control: Artificial Boundary Conditions
arxiv-2403-14436.creator: Ales Wodecki, Jakub Marecek, Vyacheslav Kungurtsev, Pavel Eichler, Georgios Korpas, Philip Intallura
arxiv-2403-14436.description: Abstract The problem of quantum state preparation is one of the main challenges in achieving the quantum advantage. Furthermore, classically, for multi-level problems, our ability to solve the corresponding quantum optimal control problems is rather limited. The ability of the latter to feed into the former may result in significant progress in quantum computing.

arxiv-2404-03602.title: Evaluating LLMs at Detecting Errors in LLM Responses

arxiv-2404-03602.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ryo Kamoi 1, Sarkar Snigdha Sarathi Das 1, Renze Lou 1, Jihyun Janice Ahn 1. However, little research has been conducted on error detection of LLM responses.

arxiv-2404-18163.title: Thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum entropy production
arxiv-2404-18163.creator: Domingos S. P. Salazar
arxiv-2404-18163.description: Abstract In quantum thermodynamics, entropy production is usually defined in terms of the quantum relative entropy between two states. We derive a lower bound for the quantum entropy production in terms of the mean and variance of quantum observables, which we will refer to as a thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR) for the entropy production.

pmc-11728630.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Aflatoxin B1 is a prevalent secondary hazardous metabolite generated by fungus present in feed ingredients and the surrounding environment: enzymes are currently being recognized as an efficient and promising approach to reducing the associated risks. The objective of this study was to assess the effects of varying doses of enzyme complexes on several parameters in laying hens that were exposed to aflatoxin. During an 8-week experiment, a total of 288 Yukou Jingfen No.6 laying hens were placed into four groups.

pmc-13426312.title: Plasma proteomics reveals molecular overlap between physical activity and dementia risk
pmc-13426312.creator: Rowan Saloner, Emily W Paolillo, Anna M VandeBunte, Claire J Cadwallader, Coty Chen, Brian T Steffen, David A Bennett, Bradley F Boeve, Howard J Rosen, Adam L Boxer, Joel H Kramer, Kaitlin B Casaletto
pmc-13426312.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Physical activity (PA) is a modifiable lifestyle behaviour associated with lower dementia risk; however, molecular pathways bridging PA-related dementia prevention are poorly understood. We leveraged large-scale plasma proteomics to identify biological signatures of objectively monitored PA and cognitive ageing in functionally intact older adults, cross-validated these signatures in independent exercise cohorts and tested associations with both symptomatic and presymptomatic stages of neurodegeneration across multiple Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD) cohorts.
